exercise1.prompt: Import math and print the area of a circle of radius 7, rounded to 2 decimal places

cases.name: prints the area rounded to two decimals
pi comes from the module rather than being typed in
the radius is squared in code
cases.describe: radius raised to the power of 2

exercise1.hint: math.pi is the full value, so multiplying it out gives a long decimal. The exercise asks for two places, which is a formatting decision you have to make somewhere.

exercise2.prompt: Use from random import randint to print a random number between 50 and 100

cases.name: randint is named in the import
randint is called with no module prefix

hiddenCases.name: prints the one number and nothing else

exercise2.hint: from ... import puts the name straight into your file. Once you have done that, writing the module name in front of it again is asking for something that is not there.

questions.prompt: After `import math`, which line finds the square root of 16?
questions.explain: A plain import gives you the module, not the names inside it. The dot is how you reach through the module to sqrt.

questions.prompt: After `from math import sqrt`, what does `math.sqrt(16)` do?
choices: Raises NameError, because math itself was never imported
questions.explain: from ... import brings in only the names you listed. The module's own name is not one of them, so math does not exist in your file.

questions.prompt: Put these lines in the order that prints the area of a circle.
questions.explain: Imports come first because the rest of the file depends on them, and every name has to exist before the line that reads it.

questions.prompt: Which of these import lines are valid Python?
questions.explain: The last one is the order other languages use. Python always names the module first: from math import sqrt.
